source.title: Towards Accurate and Efficient Sub-8-Bit Integer Training
source.authors: Wen-Jin Guo; Dong-Lai Liu; Wei-Ying Xie; Yun-Song Li; Xue-Fei Ning; Zihan Meng; Shulin Zeng; Jie Lei; Zhen-Man Fang; Yu Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure text is garbled, but the relevant results are also described in prose or tables.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies low-precision integer training and normalization, but does not measure training classification error or test any listed version’s outcome.
record.gate_note: Training accuracies and loss-landscape comparisons concern quantized normalization behavior, not the claim’s training-error measure. The paper also reports test-task accuracy, throughput, and hardware resource results; these do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study uses normalization's presumed optimization benefits to develop integer training. Its results compare normalization precision, loss-landscape smoothness, final task performance and hardware throughput. It does not compare accuracy-gain speed or learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, or measure another listed version's outcome.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that ShiftQuant improves quantized gradient estimation and fully quantized L1 normalization smooths the loss landscape, together enabling accurate and efficient low-bit training. Precision varies across tasks, some operations retain floating point, and the TGN evaluation uses 8-bit training.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes ShiftQuant and fully quantized L1 normalization for low-bitwidth training; it does not evaluate the claim’s random-initialization training-error recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Replacing quantized L2 normalization with full-precision normalization removes the reported landscape sharpness in low-precision ResNet20; proposed quantized L1 normalization also produces a qualitatively smooth landscape.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization precision and norm choice affect loss-landscape smoothness in low-precision networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully quantized L1 normalization achieves 90.40% and 91.46% accuracy on ResNet20 and ResNet38, versus 13.34% and 11.92% with fully quantized L2 normalization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fully quantized L1 normalization preserves final task accuracy much better than fully quantized L2 normalization in these low-precision ResNets.

record.problems: The normalization ablation does not state its dataset or whether accuracy is training accuracy. The loss-landscape comparison is qualitative, and no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including random or corrupted labels, and its dependence on size, stopping and regularization.
Spurious local minima in ReLU teacher-student problems and their dependence on extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain networks, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent training speed, signal and gradient propagation, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, transient loss increases and recovery, curvature trajectories, and divergence.
Accuracy-gain speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, and comparable speed and stability using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The normalization ablation's near-chance accuracies do not challenge V1 because training classification error is not reported. Hardware throughput improvements do not test V6's accuracy-gain speed. No listed version is tested.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the effects of model size, early stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU networks, spurious local minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Depth effects on training error, identity shortcuts, plain networks, and training without normalization.
Initialization comparisons and their effects on learning speed or trainable depth.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, sharpness, and divergence.
Whether adding batch normalization speeds accuracy gain or increases learning-rate tolerance; the paper compares normalization variants and reports throughput, not those outcomes.

rows.operation_detail: Compared loss landscapes for full-precision and low-precision networks with different normalization-layer precision.
rows.value: The full-precision network's loss landscape is described as less sharp than the low-precision network's.
rows.note: The paper gives a qualitative description, not a training-error measure.
rows.check: Qualitative loss-landscape smoothness does not establish any version's outcome. The comparison baseline is the low-precision network with fully quantized L2 normalization.

rows.subject: ResNet20
rows.operation_detail: Replaced quantized normalization layers with full-precision normalization layers.

conditions.value: full-precision normalization layers in low-precision network

rows.baseline: Low-precision network with quantized normalization layers: sharp loss landscape
rows.value: The paper states that the sharpness disappeared.
rows.note: Qualitative loss-landscape result; it does not measure the listed versions’ outcomes.
rows.check: Replacing normalization precision changes qualitative landscape sharpness; it does not measure accuracy-gain speed, learning-rate tolerance or stability-threshold dynamics.
